facts.statement: The study used mice to investigate how the breakdown of motor memories is connected to the removal of specific myelin sheaths by microglia.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: When cells involved in motor memory become less active, the surrounding myelin-producing cells produce less of a protective signal called CD47, which allows microglia to eat the myelin.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Removing the CD47 signal from these myelin-producing cells sped up the loss of motor memory, while boosting the signal had the opposite effect.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The research found that microglia remove myelin sheaths and synapses through separate, independent processes.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Because different kinds of memory rely on myelination, the authors suggest this process might also help explain how other types of memories fade.
facts.subject: animals
